context:
Found 2026-10-20 during the follow-up batch. Evidence is from that session; re-verify before editing. Unclaimed.

2026-10-27 21:19Z: another occurrence. Uncommitted edits to tests/unit/scripts/oracle_reviewers/conftest.py and test_attempt_loop.py in the primary clone made the pr-preflight pre-push hook refuse every worktree push until they were cleared about 13 minutes later. Not written by the docs migration session. Earlier in the docs migration, delegated agents also leaked edits into the primary clone through relative paths several times; each was reverted.

2026-10-30 data point: a delegated subagent told to work in its own worktree made its first edit (one line in docs/internal/adr/adr-site-repo-split.md) at the primary clone's absolute path. It noticed, restored the line by hand, reapplied the change in the worktree, and the primary was clean afterwards. So in-session subagents using absolute primary-clone paths are one source of primary-clone writes, not only concurrent sessions; the edit tool does not refuse such paths.

2026-10-31 data point: at 11:19:22 local, benchbox/core/benchmark_loader.py in the primary clone gained a broken partial of a change that landed 10 s later in the worktree BenchBox.wt-dep-errors (branch fix/benchmark-dependency-errors), another session. The dirty-primary guard then refused commits in every worktree until that session restored the file at 11:22:03. Same pattern as 2026-10-30: an agent edit addressed to the primary clone's absolute path just before the intended worktree edit.

2026-10-31/11-01, two more incidents: (1) a delegated worker on BenchBox PR #3886 ran its first edit command with a relative path from the primary clone's directory, so the edit landed in the primary clone; it reverted that one file with git checkout and git status was clean afterwards. (2) While another worker ran make pr-open, the primary clone held another session's uncommitted edits to benchbox/cli/commands/*.py (about host_guarded); pr-open refused until they disappeared about two minutes later.
